Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about Core Web Vitals 2026 targets and good thresholds:

## Core Web Vitals 2026 Good Thresholds

The three Core Web Vitals are Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) which measures loading speed with a good threshold of under 2.5 seconds, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) which measures responsiveness with a good threshold of under 200 milliseconds, and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) which measures visual stability with a good threshold of under 0.1.

### Detailed Threshold Breakdown

**LCP (Largest Contentful Paint):**
Good: 2.5 seconds or less, Needs Improvement: 2.6 to 4.0 seconds, Poor: Over 4.0 seconds

**INP (Interaction to Next Paint):**
Good: 200 milliseconds or less, Needs Improvement: 201 to 500 milliseconds, Poor: Over 500 milliseconds

**CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift):**
A good CLS score is less than 0.1, meaning elements stay in place as the page loads.

## Assessment Methodology

Google evaluates these at the 75th percentile of real visitor data. To pass the Core Web Vitals at least 75% of your visitors need to have a 'good' LCP, INP and CLS score in the Google CrUX dataset on the URL level.

## Key Updates for 2026

In March 2024, Google officially replaced FID with a new responsiveness metric. The current Core Web Vitals include LCP, CLS, and Interaction to Next Paint (INP). 43% of sites fail the 200 ms INP threshold, making it the most commonly failed Core Web Vital in 2026.

These metrics are essential for both SEO performance and user experience optimization.

I've found comprehensive information about Playwright smoke test suites and Next.js deployment production patterns. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Smoke Testing Overview

Smoke testing verifies your application's critical features work after deployment - it's like a quick health check for your SaaS to ensure nothing's broken before doing deeper testing.

## Smoke Test Suite Best Practices

Focus on critical paths like authentication, payments, and features users pay for, aiming for 10-20 tests covering the flows that, if broken, would prevent users from using or paying for your service. Your smoke test suite should run in under 5 minutes.

## Production Deployment Patterns

Next.js recommends running your tests against your production code to more closely resemble how your application will behave. Always run npm run build in CI so the test suite reflects how the form behaves in production, and use a production server (npm start) instead of the Next.js dev server to avoid hot-reload behaviour.

## Test Configuration

The "Smoke" project runs a small subset of tests without retries, while "Default" project runs all other tests with retries. In CI, consider running with 1 worker if you're hitting database connection limits (common with Supabase), as parallel tests are faster but can cause flakiness with shared resources.

## Key Testing Patterns

Use the Page Object Model (POM) pattern to abstract interactions with your application's pages, which makes your tests more maintainable. Test auth flows through the UI once to verify they work, but for other tests, sign in programmatically via API to save time.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Sentry with Next.js source maps, release tagging, and PII scrubbing best practices:

## Source Maps in Next.js

Upload your source maps to Sentry to enable readable stack traces in your errors. For Sentry to de-minify your stack traces you must provide both the minified files (for example, app.min.js) and the corresponding source maps.

## Release Tagging

For uploaded source maps to be located and applied, the release needs to be created by the CLI or API (and the correct artifacts uploaded with it), and the name of that newly-created release needs to be specified in your SDK configuration. Whenever you are using a distribution identifier (the dist configuration option in the SDK), the same value has to be used during source map upload. Conversely, if your source maps are getting uploaded with a dist value, the same value must be set in your SDK. To add a dist value to your uploaded source maps, use the --dist flag with sentry-cli or the dist option in our Sentry Bundler Plugins. To set the dist value in the SDK, use the dist option in your Sentry.init().

## PII Scrubbing Best Practices

We recommend using beforeSend and beforeSendTransaction in the SDKs to scrub any data before it is sent, to ensure that sensitive data never leaves the local environment.

Key areas to consider for scrubbing include:
- PII (Personally Identifiable Information) such as a user's name or email address, which post-GDPR should be on every company's mind.
- Authentication credentials, like your AWS password or key.
- A browser's pageload transaction might have a raw URL like /users/1234/details as its name (where 1234 is a user id, which may be considered PII). In most cases, our SDKs can parameterize URLs and routes successfully, that is, turn /users/1234/details into /users/:userid/details.

Sentry offers filtering or scrubbing sensitive data within the SDK, so that data is not sent to Sentry. Different SDKs have different capabilities, and configuration changes require a redeployment of your application. It also offers configuring server-side scrubbing to ensure Sentry does not store data. Configuration changes are done in the Sentry UI and apply immediately for new events, or running a local Relay on your own server between the SDK and Sentry, so that data is not sent to Sentry while configuration can still be applied without deploying.

I found comprehensive information about WCAG form error handling with ARIA. Here are the key patterns and best practices:

## Form Error Handling

WCAG 2.1 Guideline 3.3.1 requires that if an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.

## aria-describedby for Error Messages

Use the aria-describedby attribute to associate form fields with inline error messages that explain validation failures. Reference the error message ID before the helper text ID in the aria-describedby so that the error message gets announced first. Assign a unique 'id' for the container used for displaying error text and reference it via the aria-describedby attribute of the input field.

## Live Regions for Dynamic Content

Alert users to dynamic changes in content by defining live regions, especially error messages. The aria-live attribute makes it possible for assistive technologies to be notified when error messages are injected into a Live Region container, with the content automatically read by the AT without having to focus on the place where the text is displayed. Use an empty error message container element with aria-atomic=true and an aria-live property or alert role present in the DOM on page load.

## Focus Management

When a form is submitted with errors, consider programmatically moving focus to the first error message or the first field in error.

## Landmarks

All content on a webpage should be contained inside HTML regions (or ARIA landmark roles). Landmark roles programmatically identify sections of a page.

## Common ARIA Attributes for Forms

Use aria-invalid="true" on an input field when its value does not conform to the expected data format, and screen readers will announce this state.
